title: The Honey Gatherer and the Bees

pages.text: Maame Pokua lived at the edge of the forest. She gathered honey from wild hives in the tall trees. Every dry season, she carried a clay smoke pot and a woven basket to the trees.
sentences: Maame Pokua lived at the edge of the forest.
She gathered honey from wild hives in the tall trees.
Every dry season, she carried a clay smoke pot and a woven basket to the trees.
pages.alt: Maame Pokua walking calmly toward a tall forest-edge tree with a natural beehive high on a branch, carrying a small clay pot wisping gentle smoke and a woven basket.

pages.text: She took only half of the honey. “Half for me, and half for the bees,” she said. “They must eat too.”
sentences: She took only half of the honey.
“Half for me, and half for the bees,” she said.
pages.alt: Maame Pokua placing golden honeycomb into her woven basket while carefully leaving rich golden honeycomb inside the tree hive as calm honeybees hover nearby.

pages.text: Her neighbour laughed. “You are foolish! Take it all and sell it! Be rich!” Maame Pokua shook her head. “If I take it all, what will the bees live on?”
sentences: Take it all and sell it!
Be rich!” Maame Pokua shook her head.
“If I take it all, what will the bees live on?”
pages.alt: The neighbour in his green shirt laughing and gesturing greedily toward the trees while Maame Pokua calmly shakes her head holding her half-filled basket.

pages.text: The neighbour took every drop of honey from the next hive. Thick smoke filled the air, and the bees flew away to find a new home. The next year, that tree stood empty.
sentences: The neighbour took every drop of honey from the next hive.
Thick smoke filled the air, and the bees flew away to find a new home.
The next year, that tree stood empty.
pages.alt: Thick grey smoke billowing around a bare, empty hollow in a tree branch as a swarm of honeybees flies far away across the sky.

pages.text: Maame Pokua’s hives stayed full of honey. Her bees also visited the blossoms on her farm, so her fruit trees bore plenty of sweet fruit.
sentences: Maame Pokua’s hives stayed full of honey.
Her bees also visited the blossoms on her farm, so her fruit trees bore plenty of sweet fruit.
pages.alt: Sunlit farm scene where golden honeybees visit white and yellow blossoms on lush orange and mango trees laden with ripe fruit beside Maame Pokua’s thriving tree hive.

pages.text: This tale teaches a clear lesson: take only what you need, and leave enough for others. Nature gives again when we treat it fairly.
sentences: This tale teaches a clear lesson: take only what you need, and leave enough for others.
Nature gives again when we treat it fairly.
pages.alt: Maame Pokua sitting peacefully under a shady fruit tree sharing a bowl of golden honey and fruit while her humbled neighbour listens respectfully.

activities.question: How much honey does Maame Pokua take from the hive?

activities.prompt: What do you think will happen to the neighbour’s hive next year?

glossary.definition: A sweet, golden food that bees make from flower nectar.
The homes where bees live and store their honey.
Unwise; acting without thinking about what will happen later.
